title: Google rolls out a new wave of Gemini models and study tools
summary: Google's September 2026 round-up announced new Gemini models (including a new frontier model and faster 'Flash' variants), more expressive text-to-speech voices, Connected Apps inside Gemini, a Gemini app for Windows, and Gemini Notebook study tools with flashcards and video summaries.
why: Tools change monthly. Re-test your favourite prompts on new models before relying on them, and try the new study tools with the active-recall methods you learn in our courses. Check what is available in your country and plan.

title: UNESCO calls for human-centred rules as AI reshapes education
summary: At Digital Learning Week 2026 in Paris, UNESCO set out eight priorities: auditable AI with public oversight, portable data rights for students and teachers, AI that encourages independent reasoning, teacher training, age-appropriate safeguards, multilingual design, full cost accounting before adoption, and open, interoperable alternatives. UNESCO says it has supported 58 countries with AI competency frameworks.
why: Educators: this is the yardstick your school will be measured against. Use it in your AI-Enabled Classroom capstone (Education course) and your school AI policy.

title: Cameroon's National AI Strategy: one year on
summary: A Public Policy Africa review marks one year since Cameroon launched its National AI Strategy (Yaoundé, July 2025). The targets: 60,000 AI professionals trained and 12,000 direct jobs by 2040, a 0.8–1.2% GDP contribution, five centres of excellence and multilingual 'sovereign' AI solutions. The review argues that the vision is clear but the implementation is not, pointing to gaps in institutions, funding, milestones and safeguards.
why: The strategy creates demand for AI-skilled professionals in agriculture, health, education and justice. That is the skill set Team21 trains. Policy and NGO learners can use the review's gaps as a case study.

title: EU 'Digital Omnibus' delays key AI Act high-risk deadlines
summary: The EU's amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026. Transparency duties still apply from 2 August 2026, and AI-content marking applies from 2 December 2026 to systems already on the market. Obligations for stand-alone high-risk systems (e.g. in hiring and education) move to 2 December 2027, and those for AI embedded in regulated products (e.g. medical devices) move to 2 August 2028.
why: If you serve EU clients or partners, the deadlines moved but the duties did not disappear. HR, education and medical teams should keep building documentation, oversight and logging now.

title: FAR Council proposes rules to make the 'FAR Overhaul' permanent
summary: After 2025's class deviations, the FAR Council published four proposed rules revising 20 FAR parts (comment period closed 23 July 2026). Highlights: a consolidated Part 40 on supply-chain security, fewer SAM certifications, more transparency in protests, and termination settlement proposals due in 90 days instead of one year. Final rules are expected later.
why: Federal contractors and contracting officers: track which version applies to each solicitation. Our Procurement course flags these changes; always check acquisition.gov for the current text.

title: New US federal acquisition thresholds in effect
summary: The micro-purchase threshold rose to $15,000, the simplified acquisition threshold to $350,000, and the threshold for certified cost or pricing data to $2.5 million.
why: These numbers drive procurement method choices in our Procurement course exercises.
